workingTitle: HAWC maps TeV gamma rays beside the S106 star nursery
freshness: Unreviewed preprint submitted to arXiv on October 30, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: HAWC detected the previously cataloged LHAASO source 1LHAASO J2027+3657 above the team's 5-sigma threshold and found that a Planck dust-based spatial template fit better than a point source.
The HAWC analysis also found a new unidentified TeV point source, HAWC J2018+3610, elsewhere in the region.
A reanalysis of Fermi-LAT observations from August 2008 to July 2024 found extended 200 MeV to 1 TeV emission at about 11-sigma significance near S106.
A reanalysis of a roughly 45 kilosecond Chandra observation found diffuse 0.5 to 8 keV X-ray emission contributing about 10 percent of S106's total X-ray luminosity.
A single high-energy electron population can fit the X-ray through TeV spectrum if infrared photons from S106 are included, but an alternative electron-plus-proton model also fits the data.
caveats: The paper is an unreviewed preprint and its conclusions are preliminary.
The TeV source lies near rather than directly on S106, and the physical association is an interpretation rather than a direct distance measurement.
Current broadband data do not distinguish a purely leptonic model from a model with a substantial hadronic contribution.
The diffuse Chandra component may include unresolved point sources, and the Chandra exposure is a short historical snapshot compared with the long gamma-ray datasets.
Several best-fit physical parameters are correlated and poorly constrained, so the authors describe them as plausible model values rather than independent measurements.
